details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:89-111 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: Object-shaped entries in record.cves are ignored because extractPatternValue only extracts strings, so valid CVE IDs may be missed.
  WHY: All three reviewers identified the same future-compatibility gap: if npm audit returns cves entries as objects, those CVEs would be silently dropped.
- tests/test_audit_gate_identity.py:23-67 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The test file lacks edge-case coverage for case sensitivity, npm audit failure modes, malformed JSON, empty vulnerabilities, object-shaped cves, and advisory IDs in different field names.
  WHY: Both reviewers explicitly called out these missing cases as untested paths.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:276-299 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2]
  PROBLEM: runNpmAudit does not check result.status, so npm audit can exit 1 with valid JSON and still be treated as a failure path.
  WHY: The function only checks result.error, empty stdout, and JSON parse errors, so a non-zero audit exit with useful output is not handled explicitly.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:276-299 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: runNpmAudit error handling omits stderr details when spawn fails.
  WHY: It only propagates result.error.message, which loses diagnostic context that could help debug audit failures.
- tests/test_audit_gate_identity.py:23-67 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The test helper defaults audit_exit_code to 1, which reviewers described as inverted/confusing relative to real npm audit behavior.
  WHY: Two reviewers called this an inversion/usability issue, while z-ai_glm-5 said the default matches real npm audit semantics but is only confusing for maintainers.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:~160 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: normalizeAllowlistEntries accepts and lowercases any severity string without validating it against canonical npm audit severities.
  WHY: Non-canonical severity values can be baked into the identity key and fail to match npm audit output.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:~276 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: runNpmAudit is spawned without a timeout, so npm audit can hang indefinitely.
  WHY: Network issues or large repositories can stall CI if the subprocess never returns.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:~220 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: When vulnerability.via is empty or not an array, the fallback [vulnerability] path can fail to find advisoryId.
  WHY: That fallback object typically lacks advisoryId directly, so valid vulnerabilities may be reported as missing advisory id.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:105-111 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: CVE IDs in record.cves are only extracted when array elements are strings; object-shaped entries are ignored.
  WHY: If npm audit payload contains CVE information as objects in the cves array, the script will fail to extract them, potentially missing valid allowlist matches.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:276-299 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: npm audit exit code is not checked.
  WHY: If npm audit --json exits with code 1 but produces valid JSON, the script can mis-handle the result instead of processing the vulnerabilities.
- tests/test_audit_gate_identity.py:23-67
  PROBLEM: Missing edge case test coverage for case sensitivity variations in advisory IDs, various npm audit failure modes, empty vulnerabilities object, object-shaped cves array entries, and advisory IDs in different field names.
  WHY: The current test file has only the main scenarios and does not exercise those edge cases.
- tests/test_audit_gate_identity.py:23-67 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Test helper defaults audit_exit_code to 1.
  WHY: This is inverted relative to real npm audit behavior and could confuse test maintainers.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:89-104 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: CVE IDs in record.cves are only extracted when array elements are strings.
  WHY: Object entries in cves would be silently ignored, so valid CVE IDs could be missed if npm audit changes its JSON shape.
- tests/test_audit_gate_identity.py:23-67 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Missing coverage for case sensitivity edge cases, npm audit command failures, malformed JSON, and empty vulnerabilities.
  WHY: Additional edge case tests would improve robustness.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:~276 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: npm audit execution failures are not reported robustly.
  WHY: runNpmAudit() catches result.error but only includes result.error.message in the thrown error, not stderr output.
- tests/test_audit_gate_identity.py:23-67 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Test helper defaults AUDIT_GATE_FAKE_AUDIT_EXIT_CODE to 1.
  WHY: This is inverted relative to real npm audit behavior and is confusing for maintainers.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:~160 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Severity validation is permissive.
  WHY: normalizeAllowlistEntries accepts any severity string and lowercases it, which can lead to identity mismatches with npm audit's canonical severity values.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:~276 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: No timeout is set on npm audit execution.
  WHY: spawnSync is called without a timeout, so npm audit could hang indefinitely in CI or network trouble.
- workflow-templates/audit-gate/assets/scripts/security/check-npm-audit.js:~220 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Empty via array causes identity matching failure.
  WHY: When vulnerability.via is empty or not an array, the fallback vulnerability object typically lacks advisoryId directly, so valid vulnerabilities can be reported as missing advisory id.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
